title: Faizaan Fazal Khan — AI for biomedical imaging
description: I build deep-learning models that predict Alzheimer's progression from MRI and PET, and publish the parts that hold up under external validation.
positioningStatement: I build deep-learning models that predict Alzheimer's progression from MRI and PET scans.

evidence.label: conference presentations: KNGC, ICNGC, ICICPE, ICSEC

researchStatement: Alzheimer's research produces plenty of models that report strong accuracy on one dataset and say nothing about whether they'd survive contact with a different scanner, cohort, or clinician. I care about the gap between a model that looks good in a paper and one a clinician could actually act on — which means reporting uncertainty alongside predictions, testing preprocessing choices instead of assuming them, and treating explainability as a requirement, not a figure for the appendix. My work so far has moved through hippocampal segmentation, genetic and structural biomarkers, and survival modeling of MCI-to-AD conversion, each step aimed at models whose outputs come with an honest confidence attached. What I want to do next is push conformal, uncertainty-aware prediction further into the pipeline — from a single risk score toward calibrated intervals a clinician can actually weigh.
